Chapter Three Hundred Eighty-Two

Romans 13:1 — Introduction: Divine Establishment and the Four Divine Institutions

Romans 12:21 “Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good.” (ESV)
Corrected translation: Stop being conquered by evil, but conquer evil by means of the good.

Romans 13 opens a major new section of the epistle dealing with Christian responsibility to life in the world. Having established the doctrinal foundation of the Protocol Plan of God in chapters 1–11 and having traced its application to the believer's inner life in chapter 12, Paul now turns to the believer's obligations within human social structures. This chapter addresses the Royal Family Honor Code as it intersects with the laws of divine establishment — the God-ordained framework for human society from the fall of man to the second advent of Christ. Before verse 1 is examined, a thorough treatment of the doctrine of divine establishment is essential, since it governs the entire argument of Romans 13:1–7.

I. Closing Summary of Romans 12:21 — The Formula for Overcoming Evil

The final verse of chapter 12 — 'Stop being conquered by evil, but conquer evil by means of the good' — provides the transition into chapter 13. The 'good' referenced here is not moral virtue in the abstract but the specific content of the Protocol Plan of God as it operates through three categories of adjustment to the justice of God.

The X-radical of the formula encompasses the imputation of human life at physical birth and the simultaneous imputation of Adam's original sin. This instant condemnation from the justice of God is the common starting point for every member of the human race — the basis of equal condemnation that creates equal opportunity for salvation. From this starting point arises the first potential: the potentiality of salvation. The pertinent doctrine here is the gospel itself, which produces the first hope — absolute, confident assurance that faith in Christ secures eternal life. The X-radical closes with salvation adjustment to the justice of God at the moment of believing.

The Y-radical contains two judicial imputations. First, all personal sins are imputed to Christ on the cross and judged there. Second, divine righteousness is imputed to the believer at the point of salvation. These two imputations open the second stage of the plan of God: the potential for great blessing and reward at the maturity barrier. Pertinent doctrine — the content of passages such as Romans, Hebrews, Ephesians, Colossians, and Philippians — produces the second hope: absolute confidence that the moment the maturity barrier is cracked, the imputation of divine blessing follows. The Y-radical closes with maturity adjustment to the justice of God through the daily function of the Grace Apparatus for Perception.

The Z-radical encompasses the imputation of eternal life at salvation together with the imputation of temporal blessing, producing the third potential: blessing and reward at the Judgment Seat of Christ. Pertinent doctrine plus undeserved suffering generates the third hope — confident assurance of eternal blessing and reward that glorifies God. The sum of these three categories is the good that conquers evil.

Evil as a category will receive detailed treatment beginning around verse 4 of this chapter. The critical preliminary observation is that evil was not judged at the cross — only personal sin was. Good and evil together constitute the policy of Satan as ruler of this world and the operational principle of the old sin nature. The good of the Protocol Plan of God is the only force in human history capable of defeating this system.

II. Introduction to Romans 13 — Christian Responsibility to Life

Chapter 13 addresses Christian responsibility across two domains simultaneously: the laws of divine establishment, which govern every human being regardless of spiritual status, and the Royal Family Honor Code, which governs the believer specifically. The first seven verses deal primarily with establishment law and principle. Understanding this chapter requires a prior command of the doctrine of divine establishment and the four divine institutions that constitute its structural framework.

III. Doctrine of Divine Establishment

A. Definition and Description

There are two sources of integrity in human life. The unbeliever receives integrity through observation of the laws of divine establishment; the product of that integrity is morality. Morality is designed for the human race in general and specifically serves the unbeliever by enabling the principle of integrity — live and let live. The believer possesses both establishment morality and the infinitely higher standard of the Royal Family Honor Code. Christianity does not stand apart from establishment responsibility; rather, the believer operates under both systems simultaneously.

Point 1. God has ordained certain laws for the survival and freedom of the human race throughout the course of human history. The human race cannot be perpetuated unless significant segments of it observe these laws. These laws are as foundational to life in the human race as the law of gravity is to physical existence on earth.

Point 2. The laws of divine establishment are designed and directed toward both the believer and the unbeliever in the Lord Jesus Christ. They are universal in scope, not restricted to those who are regenerate.

Point 3. The divine laws of establishment operate from the fall of man to the second advent of Christ. They will continue to function during the millennial reign of Christ under an absolute monarchy, though with certain modifications appropriate to perfect environment. For practical purposes, the operating frame is the fall of man to the second advent.

Point 4. These laws directly affect freedom, civilization, legitimate authority, evangelism, the spiritual growth of believers, and the perpetuation of the human race and of history itself.

Point 5. The laws of divine establishment define freedom in terms of three categories: privacy, property, and authority. Privacy protects the individual in the exercise of personal volition, including the freedom to approach the Word of God without social coercion or spiritual bullying. Gossip, maligning, judging, and vindictive criticism are violations of this privacy and must be addressed to maintain the integrity of any assembly committed to doctrinal instruction. Property establishes the right of individuals to possess and retain what is lawfully theirs. The Royal Family Honor Code reinforces this establishment principle: the personal property of others is inviolable. Authority is the structural prerequisite for freedom. There is no freedom — civic, spiritual, or personal — without recognized and functioning authority. Traffic laws and their enforcement illustrate the principle at the level of daily life: thousands of drivers with varying skills share the same roads in freedom only because all submit to a common authority structure. The same principle operates in the local church, where recognition of communicative authority is the prerequisite for the perception of Bible doctrine.

Point 6. Both the privacy of the individual and the function of legitimate authority are necessary for the operation of human freedom. Freedom apart from authority is anarchy; authority apart from privacy is tyranny. The two are inseparable.

Point 7. The four divine institutions are the structural basis for the stability of the human race in history. These institutions are: (1) human volition, (2) marriage, (3) family, and (4) nationalism. Each will be examined in turn.

B. Divine Institution Number One — Human Volition

The soul is divinely prepared as the permanent container of human life. The body houses the soul; the soul houses human life. Human life is imputed by the justice of God to the soul at the moment of physical birth — not in the womb, but at birth. Once imputed, human life cannot be removed from the soul by any force in the universe. This may be termed the doctrine of human security: every member of the human race possesses human life permanently, regardless of circumstances. Physical death does not terminate human life; it merely separates the soul from the body. The soul — with human life intact — departs either to the presence of the Lord or to a place of separation from God, according to the individual's relationship to Christ.

For the believer, a second category of life exists alongside human life: eternal life. Eternal life requires a permanent home just as human life does. That home is regeneration — prepared by God the Holy Spirit at the moment of faith in Christ. Regeneration is not primarily a synonym for the salvation experience as a whole; its specific function is to serve as the permanent container for eternal life, just as the soul serves as the permanent container for human life. Neither human life nor eternal life can be forfeited by any sin — including what some mistakenly identify as an unpardonable sin. The one unpardonable sin is the rejection of Christ, but that sin forecloses the opportunity for salvation; it does not threaten the eternal life of those who have already believed. Physical death for the believer is a change of residence, not a loss of life.

The possession of two categories of life means the believer operates under two corresponding sets of laws: the laws of divine establishment governing the human race, and the Royal Family Honor Code governing the royal family of God. The unbeliever operates under establishment law alone. The error common to new believers is the confusion of the two systems — treating establishment morality as the equivalent of spiritual maturity, or assuming that moral compliance under establishment produces divine blessing. It does not. Establishment morality produces, at best, good citizenship. Spiritual maturity — and the imputed blessings that attend it — comes only through sustained doctrine intake, the daily function of the Grace Apparatus for Perception, and cracking the maturity barrier. When both sets of laws are properly distinguished and applied, the result is a believer of genuine integrity, spiritual common sense, capacity for love, and readiness to receive divine blessing.

The soul consists of several components that work in coordination: self-consciousness (awareness of one's own existence and identity), mentality (the cognitive faculty that processes information), and volition (the faculty of decision, positive and negative). The left lobe of the mentality — called in the New Testament

The soul consists of several components that work in coordination: self-consciousness (awareness of one's own existence and identity), mentality (the cognitive faculty that processes information), and volition (the faculty of decision, positive and negative). The left lobe of the mentality — designated in the New Testament as nous (νοῦς) — processes incoming information. The right lobe — designated kardia (καρδία) — stores doctrine in the frame of reference, the memory center, vocabulary and categorical storage, and the conscience (norms and standards). Emotion responds to the content of the right lobe; it is designed as a responder, not a ruler. Under divine institution number one it is volition — not emotion — that functions as the authoritative faculty governing the soul's operation.

Human volition requires freedom and privacy for its proper function. God provides this privacy structurally: the soul is housed in the skull, screened from external observation by bone, tissue, and features. No one has direct access to the contents of another person's soul. This architectural privacy is the physical basis for the principle of soul privacy as a law of divine establishment. No government, no social group, and no religious organization has legitimate authority to coerce or monitor the private exercise of individual volition.

The principle may be stated as follows: divine establishment under divine institution number one provides both freedom and privacy for those who do not violate common or criminal law. The moment an individual's actions violate the law — robbery, murder, assault — the privacy protection of divine establishment is forfeited, and legitimate governmental authority may and must act. This is not an infringement of freedom but the structural defense of the freedom of all others.

Individuals within the human race are not born equal in capacity, intelligence, or circumstance. The equality of divine establishment is not an equality of outcome or ability, but an equality of freedom of choice: every person possessing normal human faculties has the right to pursue a course of action compatible with personal aspiration and ability, so long as that course does not violate the freedom of others. No government has the authority to suppress legitimate personal motivation by imposing artificial equality of outcome.

At the point of God-consciousness, every member of the human race with normal mental faculties has the option of positive or negative volition toward the existence of God. At the point of gospel hearing, every individual has the uncoerced right to believe in Christ or to reject him. This decision belongs entirely to the individual and must not be subjected to social pressure, emotional manipulation, or what is commonly called 'follow-up.' The concept of follow-up — pressuring a new or recent convert to attend services, adopt behaviors, or conform to expectations — is a violation of privacy and an importation of social coercion into the spiritual life. The Lord himself provides for those who are positive toward doctrine by bringing them to the right pastor and the right local church. He provides for those who are negative through divine discipline. The freedom of the soul under divine institution number one is the structural basis for true evangelism; true evangelism does not coerce, manipulate, or crowd the individual's volition.

Note the single historical exception to the freedom-requires-privacy-and-authority principle: the Roman Empire. The Empire maintained a large slave population roughly equal in number to its free citizenry. Both categories responded to the gospel in approximately equal proportions. The Apostle Paul, under the ministry of the Holy Spirit, did not call for the abolition of slavery as a social institution. Rather, he instructed slaves to remain in their condition — they were God's free persons in the spiritual domain — and instructed free persons to understand themselves as God's bondservants. The reason this exception held is that the Roman establishment system, even under slavery, maintained sufficient structural freedom for slaves to assemble, worship, and advance spiritually. Social action was not the apostolic agenda; doctrinal advance within whatever structural context the believer occupied was. This exception does not nullify the principle; it demonstrates that spiritual freedom and maturity adjustment are possible even in the absence of full civic freedom, provided the establishment framework permits assembly and doctrinal instruction.

C. Divine Institution Number Two — Marriage

Marriage is a divine institution for the entire human race, not a specifically Christian institution. Its authority and validity derive from creation, not from religious ceremony or ecclesiastical sanction. The relevant scriptural foundations are Genesis 1:26–27; 2:18–25; 5:1–2; 1 Corinthians 7:2–4.

The principle is monogamy: a permanent relationship between one man and one woman. This is the order established by God at the creation of man, prior to the fall, when man was still perfect and ruled the world rather than Satan. The Lord himself declared in Genesis 2:18, 'It is not good that man should be alone,' and responded by constructing a right woman for the first man. In the original Hebrew, the woman is called

The principle is monogamy: a permanent relationship between one man and one woman. This is the order established by God at creation, prior to the fall, when man was still in an unfallen state. The Lord himself declared in Genesis 2:18, 'It is not good that man should be alone,' and provided accordingly. In the original Hebrew, the man is called 'ish (אִישׁ), and the woman was called 'ishah (אִשָּׁה) — taken from man, part of man. The name Eve came later, assigned by Adam after the fall and after her salvation. This relationship was established in the garden in perfection and has never been canceled by the fall, by human failure, or by any subsequent generation's deviation from the standard. The failures of individuals do not invalidate the institution; they reflect human weakness. Violations of a principle never change the principle.

Monogamy excludes homosexual union and lesbian union categorically. These are departures from the design established at the creation of the human race and maintained throughout the laws of divine establishment.

The analogy to the monogamous relationship is developed in Ephesians 5:26–33. Under the authority structure of divine establishment, the husband holds the authority in the marriage. This is not conditioned on superior intelligence, wisdom, or competence. It is structural, ordained by God, and it has not been altered by any failure in any marriage in history. Additional references governing the institution of marriage: 1 Corinthians 7:9; 1 Timothy 5:14; Ephesians 5:22–23, 28, 31, 33; Hebrews 13:4.

Marriage is the beginning of authority in adult life outside the self. Prior to marriage, the only authority structure operating in the individual is internal — the authority of volition over the other faculties of the soul. Marriage introduces the first external organizational authority. It is also the basis for the stability of society and the formation of civilization. Marriage rejects the premises of anarchy, revolutionary communal living, and promiscuousness. It establishes the home as a protected domain within which the third divine institution — the family — will operate. The correct sequence in marriage is rational evaluation before emotional commitment; emotion that precedes rational assessment produces the conditions for the most common and most damaging category of personal failure in human experience.

D. Divine Institution Number Three — Family

The third divine institution is the family. Parents exercise authority over children; children possess only such freedom as parents permit. The degree of freedom extended to children must be calibrated to their level of development and responsibility. Excessive permissiveness in child-rearing does not produce freedom — it produces individuals who arrive at adulthood without the capacity for authority orientation, and who therefore function destructively within society. Children are members of the human race in a provisional status — human beings without the full portfolio of civic freedom — until they reach adulthood under the authority and formation of the family.

E. Divine Institution Number Four — Nationalism

The fourth divine institution is nationalism — the organization of the human race into distinct national entities with defined borders, systems of law, and governmental authority. Nationalism as a divine institution is the direct subject of Romans 13:1–7. Practical applications of this institution include compliance with taxation, observance of law, and — for males — the embrace rather than evasion of military service. These applications will be examined in detail when the text of Romans 13 is reached. The full doctrinal complexity of nationalism, including its relationship to the five cycles of discipline and the rise and fall of national entities in history, will be developed as the passage demands.

Conclusions from Chapter Three Hundred Eighty-Two

1. Evil is not overcome by social action or moral effort, but by the full operation of the Protocol Plan of God across its three categories of adjustment to the justice of God. The 'good' of Romans 12:21 is the sum of salvation adjustment, maturity adjustment, and the eschatological blessings that attend ultra-supergrace — not generic virtue.

2. Evil was not judged at the cross; only personal sin was. Good and evil remain the contested domain of the angelic conflict throughout human history. The believer's weapon in this conflict is doctrine — specifically the doctrine that constitutes the content of the Protocol Plan of God.

3. Romans 13:1–7 addresses divine establishment law, not merely civic ethics. The passage cannot be understood apart from a thorough grasp of the four divine institutions and the authority structures embedded in each.

4. The laws of divine establishment are universal, operating from the fall of man to the second advent, and governing both believer and unbeliever. They define freedom in terms of privacy, property, and authority — three categories that must all be present for any form of freedom to function.

5. Human volition is the primary faculty of divine institution number one. It requires privacy and freedom for its proper operation. The structural privacy of the soul — housed in the skull, inaccessible to direct external observation — is the physical correlate of this legal privacy. Any coercion of individual volition, including the coercion of religious 'follow-up,' is a violation of establishment principle.

6. Human life is imputed at birth, not in the womb, and is permanently resident in the soul. It cannot be removed by any means or by any agent. Eternal life, similarly, is permanent once imputed, housed in the regenerate state prepared by God the Holy Spirit. Physical death for the believer is a change of residence, not a loss of either category of life.

7. The believer operates under two simultaneous legal frameworks: the laws of divine establishment (governing all human beings) and the Royal Family Honor Code (governing the royal family of God specifically). Confusion of the two — equating establishment morality with spiritual maturity, or expecting divine blessing as the reward of civic virtue — is a fundamental error that must be corrected by rightly dividing the word of truth.

8. Marriage is a divine institution for the human race, not a Christian institution. Its authority derives from creation, not from ecclesiastical ceremony. Monogamy — one man and one woman in a permanent relationship — is the creation order and has never been canceled by human failure or by cultural deviation. The authority of the husband over the wife is structural and unchanging.

9. The four divine institutions — volition, marriage, family, nationalism — constitute the structural framework for the stability of human civilization. Each embodies a specific authority relationship. The breakdown of any one institution produces corresponding social disorder. The health of a national entity depends on the integrity with which all four are observed.

10. Christianity is compatible with many forms of government, but not with the absence of the laws of divine establishment. The Roman historical example demonstrates that even slavery, when embedded in a sufficiently stable establishment framework, need not prevent evangelism or spiritual maturity. Social action is not the apostolic agenda; doctrinal advance is.

nous νοῦς nous — mind, left lobe of the soul In New Testament usage, the cognitive faculty that receives and processes information. The left lobe of the mentality, which takes in data before it is transferred to the right lobe (kardia) for storage and application.

Chapter Three Hundred Eighty-Three

Romans 13:1 — Laws of Divine Establishment: Divine Institutions Three and Four

Romans 13:1 “Let every person be subject to the governing authorities. For there is no authority except from God, and those that exist have been instituted by God.” (ESV)
Corrected translation: Let every soul be in subordination to superior authorities. For there is no authority except from God, and those which exist have been appointed by God.

Romans 13 is one of the most concentrated expressions of the laws of divine establishment in all of Scripture. Before the exegesis of the chapter itself can proceed, the theological framework that undergirds it must be established. This chapter continues a point-by-point study of the divine establishment laws that provide the context for Paul's instruction regarding civil authority. The present chapter covers divine institution number three (the family) and divine institution number four (the nation), both of which are essential to understanding why Paul commands subordination to governing authorities.

I. The Plan of God: Three Stages

The plan of God for the human race operates in three stages, each with its own confidence and hope that leads to action. These stages are represented schematically as X, Y, and Z.

Stage One: The X Radical — Physical Birth and the First Potential

The X radical encompasses the imputation of human life at the moment of birth combined with the imputation of Adam's original sin. These two simultaneous imputations produce the condition in which every human being enters the world: possessing true human life yet standing condemned. Human life is imputed by the justice of God to its divinely prepared home, the human soul. Adam's original sin is imputed to the genetically formed old sin nature. This is the sole basis for the condemnation of the human race. Personal sins, by contrast, are never imputed to the individual for condemnation — they were imputed to Christ on the cross and judged there.

From this condition of condemnation the justice of God is able to provide great blessing. The first potential arising from the X radical is the potential of salvation. The first hope is the absolute assurance that the moment one believes in Jesus Christ, eternal life is received. Within the X radical the laws of divine establishment begin to operate, making possible the existence of human freedom within the framework of authority and under the protection of privacy. The first plus — the transition to Stage Two — is salvation adjustment to the justice of God through personal faith in the Lord Jesus Christ.

Stage Two: The Y Radical — Judicial Imputation and the Second Potential

The Y radical contains two judicial imputations. First, the imputation of all personal sins to Jesus Christ on the cross — the saving work of Christ. Second, the imputation of divine righteousness to the believer at the moment of salvation. The possession of God's righteousness creates the basis for the next stage: righteousness demands righteousness; justice demands justice; what righteousness demands, justice executes. The divine righteousness resident in the believer becomes the target for the imputation of divine blessing, which glorifies God forever.

The second potential is the potential of the imputation of divine blessing in time as the means of glorifying the Lord Jesus Christ. The second hope is absolute confidence that when enough doctrine has been received to crack the maturity barrier, the sixth imputation of divine blessing — in six categories — will be received as the tactical victory in the angelic conflict. The second plus is maturity adjustment to the justice of God. Within the Y radical the operative standard rises from establishment law to the Royal Family Honor Code, which adds to but does not set aside establishment.

Stage Three: The Z Radical — Ultra-Supergrace and the Third Potential

The Z radical is the final stage of the Christian life on earth, the zone in which the mature believer operates. The imputation of eternal life and salvation combined with the imputation of blessings in time at the point of maturity produces the third potential: great blessing and reward in eternity. The third hope is absolute confidence of reward at the judgment seat of Christ. The third stage includes undeserved suffering designed to maintain eternal perspective.

The formula X plus Y plus Z equals the plan of God — the good of Romans 8:28. All things work together for the purpose of the good because the plan proceeds in three ordered stages, each with its confidence, its hope, and its required action.

II. The Royal Family Honor Code

Once a person believes in the Lord Jesus Christ and enters the Y radical, the operative standard expands from establishment law alone to include the Royal Family Honor Code. The believer operates under two identities simultaneously.

First, as a royal ambassador, the believer represents the Lord Jesus Christ on the earth. Production — witnessing, giving, prayer, service under one's spiritual gift — flows from this identity. However, no production, no sacrifice, no function under a spiritual gift produces blessing from God. Blessing does not come through works, personality, morality, asceticism, or any form of self-sacrifice.

Second, as a royal priest, the believer approaches God directly. All blessing comes from doctrine resident in the soul, accumulated through the daily function of the Grace Apparatus for Perception (GAP). Doctrine provides capacity for blessing. When maximum doctrine has been received in the soul, blessing begins to flow in the six categories of the sixth imputation. The combination of establishment law and the Royal Family Honor Code produces the historical impact of freedom for any nation.

III. Divine Institution Three: The Family

The third divine institution is the family. Its function is to bridge the gap between the helplessness of physical birth and the responsibilities of adult life under the laws of establishment.

A. Physical Birth and the Dual Imputation

Physical birth and the simultaneous imputation of human life and Adam's original sin leaves the infant both helpless and condemned. Human life is not present in the womb; it is imputed by the justice of God at birth to the human soul. Adam's original sin is imputed to the genetically formed old sin nature. All personal sins accumulate but are never imputed to the individual for condemnation — they were imputed to Christ on the cross and judged. This is why Christ is the issue in salvation and why the Scripture declares, 'Believe on the Lord Jesus Christ and thou shalt be saved.'

B. Parental Authority as the Basis for Life Preparation

God has provided parents to protect, care for, nourish, provide for, train, and discipline children in order to prepare them for life. Parental authority is therefore the basis for preparing children for a normal life. Permissiveness destroys this preparation. Recognition of authority and orientation to the principles of life must be inculcated in the home; they cannot be deferred to any educational system. Parents hold the right and privilege of this inculcation.

C. The Content of Authority Training

The highest expression of parental love is discipline administered in order to instill character. Children must be trained to respect the privacy of others, to respect property, to respect the rights of others, and to understand and operate within the framework of freedom without abusing it. Authority training — distinct from and higher than mere behavioral conditioning — equips children with objectivity, respect for law and order, and a well-founded patriotism that includes willingness to defend national freedoms against external enemies.

In addition to establishment training, Christian parents bear a spiritual responsibility. They are to evangelize their children and provide pre-doctrinal training, as taught in Deuteronomy 6:6–9 and Deuteronomy 7–9. It is the responsibility of parents to instill respect for the Word of God and for the teaching authority of the pastor-teacher (Hebrews 13:7, 17). Whatever personal reservations a parent may hold about a given pastor, these are not to be communicated to children, who require an unobstructed orientation to authority in order to be functional in life.

IV. Divine Institution Four: The Nation

The fourth divine institution is the nation. It exists because, prior to the millennium, the entire human race cannot be brought under one rule without self-destruction. Internationalism in any form — civic, political, or religious — is therefore prohibited for this stage of history. Every human being possesses an old sin nature; the division of humanity into distinct national entities is the divine safeguard that perpetuates history until its logical conclusion.

A. The Origin of Nations

The divine judgment of the original internationalist project — the Tower of Babel recorded in Genesis 11 — divided the human race into distinct nations. The original definition of national entities was based on racial, geographical, and linguistic norms. The pertinent Scripture references authorizing nations while prohibiting international superstructures include Genesis 10:5, Deuteronomy 32:8, and Acts 17:26–28.

B. The Myth of Racial Purity

As history progressed, true racial distinctions were obliterated in the rise of civilization. Racial purity is a myth in any historically developed national entity. The populations of Western Europe illustrate this clearly: the English are a mixture of Teutonic, Celtic, Scandinavian, and other peoples; the French, whose very name derives from the Frankish Teutonic peoples, are largely of Teutonic origin despite cultural assumptions to the contrary; the Spanish show Celtic, Teutonic (Visigothic and Ostrogothic), and Iberian strands; the Italians reflect the passage of virtually every major civilization through the peninsula over two millennia. Racial ideology used as a basis for political power, as in the case of National Socialism in Germany, is a myth employed as political expediency.

C. The Standard of a Nation Under Divine Establishment

Nations that follow the norms and standards of divine establishment exhibit the following characteristics. There is no such thing as a Christian nation — there are Christians within nations — but nations can align themselves with establishment norms and thereby function as client nations of God.

First, interior protection of freedom through an honorable system of law enforcement and jurisprudence. The principle of law enforcement is essential to the preservation of individual freedom and privacy. A corrupt individual within a law enforcement institution does not invalidate the institution any more than a dishonest employee invalidates the corporation employing him. The response to corruption is prosecution and removal — not abolition of the institution.

The inherited jurisprudential tradition of Western nations — drawing on principles from the Mosaic law, Roman law, and Anglo-Saxon common law — includes the prohibition of double jeopardy, the presumption of innocence, and the exclusion of hearsay testimony as the sole basis for conviction. These are not merely legal conventions but reflections of biblical standards of justice.

Second, exterior protection of freedom through an honorable military establishment. All freedom that any national entity has ever possessed was secured through military victory. The military functions as the exterior protection of national freedom in the same way that law enforcement functions as the interior protection. Both are among the oldest and most honorable of human institutions.

Third, a government of whatever constitutional form — monarchy, oligarchy, or republic — that protects the freedoms and rights of its citizens without abusing its power to destroy those freedoms. The United States was constituted as a republic, not a democracy. Democracy, which is governed by the opinion of the numerical majority, is incompatible with the standards of divine establishment. Christianity can function under virtually any form of government except pure democracy, because what the majority of people think at any given moment is of no consequence as a standard of truth or justice. Democracy is proximate to anarchy; no democracy in history has long survived without degenerating toward it.

Fourth, an economy based on free enterprise and capitalism. Under this standard, the investor and management hold the sole right to formulate business policy within a company or corporation. Neither central government, labor organizations, nor criminal enterprises have the right to superimpose policy on private business. Sound management invariably takes care of its own productive members; the imposition of external control destroys both productivity and the self-respect of those who participate in the system.

Fifth, a system of common law that prohibits criminal action and thereby protects the freedom, rights, life, and property of individuals. Critically, law must not be distorted into an instrument for solving social problems. Law is designed to restrain criminal action. Legislation that coerces private associations, invades individual rights, or redistributes personal property under the name of the common good exceeds the proper function of law and becomes an instrument of oppression.

Sixth, a common culture that reflects the spiritual life, morality, corporate spirit, nobility, integrity, and patriotism of the nation. A nation's culture is the outward expression of the interior values of its people.

Seventh, a government administration that exercises its power without abusing it to destroy freedom — a system of mutual authority that encourages freedom rather than restrains it, maintains an honorable military on a realistic basis, enforces law and order without the destruction of human freedom, and administers taxation, law enforcement, and jurisprudence within its proper scope.

V. Establishment and Evangelism

The laws of divine establishment are not ends in themselves. They are designed to protect human freedom for the purpose of genuine evangelism. Where positive volition toward the gospel exists in a population, establishment provides the framework within which that volition can be freely exercised. Where negative volition exists, establishment provides protection from coercion.

The individual citizen must be free to accept or reject Christ as Savior without interference. Evangelism that uses public pressure — requiring people to raise their hands, walk forward in a crowd, or make a public declaration — violates both human privacy and the principle of non-meritorious faith. The merit in salvation lies entirely with the object, the Lord Jesus Christ, not with any action of the one believing. True faith is an act of the will in the privacy of the soul.

The state must neither coerce acceptance of Christ nor punish rejection of Him. No church has the authority to persecute those who reject Christ as Savior. The state must never adopt an official religion supported by public taxation; all religious bodies must be free from taxation and free from state support equally. The separation of church and state is therefore not an anti-religious principle but a foundational establishment principle protecting the very freedom that makes genuine evangelism possible.

The alternative is visible in the historical record of regions where a state church held coercive power. The dominance of a state church destroys religious freedom; the resulting resentment and reaction leave populations unable to conceptualize an alternative other than the opposite extreme. The doctrine of John 3:36 frames the issue with absolute clarity: 'He that believeth on the Son hath everlasting life; he that believeth not the Son shall not see life, but the wrath of God abideth on him.' The choice is binary and entirely private. Establishment exists to ensure that choice is genuinely free.

Conclusions from Chapter Three Hundred Eighty-Three

1. The plan of God operates in three sequential stages. Stage One (X radical) establishes the human condition at physical birth and the potential of salvation. Stage Two (Y radical) encompasses the judicial imputations of salvation and the believer's advance toward maturity. Stage Three (Z radical) is the supergrace life with its eternal rewards. Each stage carries its own hope — its own absolute confidence — that generates appropriate action.

2. All blessing from God flows from the justice of God to the righteousness of God. Justice and righteousness together constitute divine integrity. The justice of God is the pipeline through which all blessing is dispensed. No blessing comes through works, personality, morality, or sacrifice. Blessing comes through doctrine resident in the soul, which provides capacity for the divine blessing that justice imputes to righteousness.

3. The family is the third divine institution, designed to bridge helplessness at birth and responsibility in adult life. Parental authority is the essential mechanism of this bridge. Authority training — instilling respect for the privacy of others, for property, for law and order, and for legitimate government — must begin in the home. It cannot be deferred. Christian parents bear an additional responsibility to evangelize their children and to model respect for the teaching authority of the Word of God.

4. The nation is the fourth divine institution, designed to protect human freedom. The division of humanity into distinct national entities at Babel was a divine judgment against internationalism and a protective design for the perpetuation of history. Internationalism in any form — political, civic, or religious — is outside the authorization of divine establishment for this stage of history.

5. Racial ideology has no foundation in the historical record. As civilization developed, racial distinctions were obliterated through migration, conquest, and intermarriage. The populations of every historically developed nation are composites. Racial purity is a myth; its use as political ideology is a form of expediency that has no support from the Word of God.

6. Nations aligned with divine establishment exhibit seven identifiable characteristics. These are: interior protection of freedom through honorable law enforcement and jurisprudence; exterior protection through an honorable military; a government that protects rather than destroys freedom; a free-enterprise economy; a system of common law that restrains crime without exceeding its proper function; a national culture reflecting integrity and patriotism; and a government administration that exercises authority within its proper limits.

7. Law must not be weaponized as an instrument for solving social problems. The proper function of law is to restrain criminal action and protect the freedom, rights, life, and property of individuals. Legislation that invades private associations, coerces private economic decisions, or redistributes personal property under the claim of advancing the common good exceeds the proper scope of law and becomes a form of oppression.

8. Democracy is incompatible with the standards of divine establishment. A republic — a government of enumerated powers and constitutional limits — is compatible with Scripture. Democracy, governed by numerical majority opinion, is not. Majority opinion carries no authority as a standard of truth or justice. Every democracy in history has tended toward anarchy without the restraining structure of constitutional government.

9. The laws of divine establishment exist to protect the freedom that makes genuine evangelism possible. Where people are free — free to accept Christ, free to reject Him, free from coercion in either direction — the gospel can be heard and believed in the privacy of the soul. Evangelism that depends on public pressure or crowd psychology violates both human privacy and the principle of non-meritorious faith. The state must neither coerce religious belief nor punish religious choice. Separation of church and state is a biblical establishment principle, not an anti-religious one.

10. The separation of church and state protects the integrity of both institutions. A state religion always destroys human freedom. Where a church holds coercive state power, it destroys the very freedom of conscience that genuine faith requires. History demonstrates that populations long subjected to coercive state religion become unable to conceive of genuine religious freedom and are therefore susceptible to the opposite extreme. Establishment law, properly applied, prevents this outcome.

Glossary

Glossary

Term Greek / Transliteration Definition
Divine establishment The body of divine laws, analogous to laws of nature, that govern the existence and stability of the human race on earth. These laws make possible human freedom within the framework of authority. They operate in the X radical of the plan of God and apply to believers and unbelievers alike.
Divine institution One of four foundational structures ordained by God for the perpetuation and governance of the human race: (1) individual volition, (2) marriage, (3) the family, (4) the nation. Each divine institution carries its own system of authority designed to protect human freedom.
GAP Grace Apparatus for Perception The Spirit-enabled process by which a believer receives and internalizes Bible doctrine under the teaching of a pastor-teacher. The daily function of GAP is the means by which doctrine accumulates in the soul, providing the capacity for divine blessing.
Maturity barrier The threshold of spiritual maturity reached through sustained intake of Bible doctrine over time. Cracking the maturity barrier triggers the sixth imputation — the imputation of divine blessing in six categories as the tactical victory in the angelic conflict.
Client nation A national entity that aligns itself with the norms and standards of divine establishment, thereby receiving divine blessing and serving as a base for evangelism and the communication of Bible doctrine. There are no Christian nations as such; a client nation is an establishment nation that contains a functioning pivot of mature believers.
Pivot The body of mature believers within a national entity whose adjustment to the justice of God sustains divine blessing on that nation. The size and health of the pivot determines the degree to which a nation continues to receive logistical grace at the national level.
Royal Family Honor Code The higher standard of conduct operative in the Y and Z radicals of the plan of God. It adds to but does not set aside the laws of divine establishment. The believer operates under two identities: royal ambassador (representing Christ in the world) and royal priest (approaching God directly through doctrine and prayer).
Imputation The divine act of crediting something to someone's account. Seven key imputations structure the plan of God: (1) human life to the soul at birth; (2) Adam's original sin to the old sin nature; (3) personal sins to Christ on the cross; (4) divine righteousness to the believer at salvation; (5) eternal life to the believer at salvation; (6) divine blessing to the believer at maturity; (7) rewards and blessings at the judgment seat of Christ.
Old sin nature (OSN) The sin capacity inherited at physical birth through the male genetic line. Adam's original sin is imputed to the genetically formed old sin nature. Personal sins accumulate in the OSN but are not imputed to the individual for condemnation — they were judged in Christ on the cross.
Salvation adjustment The instantaneous, once-for-all act by which a person is brought into right relationship with the justice of God through personal faith in the Lord Jesus Christ. Non-meritorious: the merit resides entirely in the object of faith, not in the act of believing.
Maturity adjustment The progressive advance of the believer toward spiritual maturity through the daily intake of Bible doctrine via GAP. Culminates in cracking the maturity barrier and receiving the sixth imputation of divine blessing. Represents the second major adjustment to the justice of God in the plan of God.

The pertinent Scripture references authorizing nations while prohibiting international superstructures include Genesis 10:5, Deuteronomy 32:8, and Acts 17:26–28.

B. The Myth of Racial Purity

As history progressed, true racial distinctions were obliterated in the rise of civilization. Racial purity is a myth in any historically developed national entity. The populations of Western Europe illustrate this clearly: the English are a mixture of Teutonic, Celtic, Scandinavian, and other peoples; the French, whose very name derives from the Frankish Teutonic peoples, are largely of Teutonic origin despite cultural assumptions to the contrary; the Spanish show Celtic, Teutonic (Visigothic and Ostrogothic), and Iberian strands; the Italians reflect the passage of virtually every major civilization through the peninsula over two millennia. Racial ideology used as a basis for political power, as in the case of National Socialism in Germany, is a myth employed as political expediency.

C. The Standard of a Nation Under Divine Establishment

Nations that follow the norms and standards of divine establishment exhibit the following characteristics. There is no such thing as a Christian nation — there are Christians within nations — but nations can align themselves with establishment norms and thereby function as client nations of God.

First, interior protection of freedom through an honorable system of law enforcement and jurisprudence. The principle of law enforcement is essential to the preservation of individual freedom and privacy. A corrupt individual within a law enforcement institution does not invalidate the institution any more than a dishonest employee invalidates the corporation employing him. The response to corruption is prosecution and removal — not abolition of the institution.

The inherited jurisprudential tradition of Western nations — drawing on principles from the Mosaic law, Roman law, and Anglo-Saxon common law — includes the prohibition of double jeopardy, the presumption of innocence, and the exclusion of hearsay testimony as the sole basis for conviction. These are not merely legal conventions but reflections of biblical standards of justice.

Second, exterior protection of freedom through an honorable military establishment. All freedom that any national entity has ever possessed was secured through military victory. The military functions as the exterior protection of national freedom in the same way that law enforcement functions as the interior protection. Both are among the oldest and most honorable of human institutions.

Third, a government of whatever constitutional form — monarchy, oligarchy, or republic — that protects the freedoms and rights of its citizens without abusing its power to destroy those freedoms. The United States was constituted as a republic, not a democracy. Democracy, which is governed by the opinion of the numerical majority, is incompatible with the standards of divine establishment. Christianity can function under virtually any form of government except pure democracy, because what the majority of people think at any given moment is of no consequence as a standard of truth or justice. Democracy is proximate to anarchy; no democracy in history has long survived without degenerating toward it.

Fourth, an economy based on free enterprise and capitalism. Under this standard, the investor and management hold the sole right to formulate business policy within a company or corporation. Neither central government, labor organizations, nor criminal enterprises have the right to superimpose policy on private business. Sound management invariably takes care of its own productive members; the imposition of external control destroys both productivity and the self-respect of those who participate in the system.

Fifth, a system of common law that prohibits criminal action and thereby protects the freedom, rights, life, and property of individuals. Critically, law must not be distorted into an instrument for solving social problems. Law is designed to restrain criminal action. Legislation that coerces private associations, invades individual rights, or redistributes personal property under the name of the common good exceeds the proper function of law and becomes an instrument of oppression.

Sixth, a common culture that reflects the spiritual life, morality, corporate spirit, nobility, integrity, and patriotism of the nation. A nation's culture is the outward expression of the interior values of its people.

Seventh, a government administration that exercises its power without abusing it to destroy freedom — a system of mutual authority that encourages freedom rather than restrains it, maintains an honorable military on a realistic basis, enforces law and order without the destruction of human freedom, and administers taxation, law enforcement, and jurisprudence within its proper scope.

V. Establishment and Evangelism

The laws of divine establishment are not ends in themselves. They are designed to protect human freedom for the purpose of genuine evangelism. Where positive volition toward the gospel exists in a population, establishment provides the framework within which that volition can be freely exercised. Where negative volition exists, establishment provides protection from coercion.

The individual citizen must be free to accept or reject Christ as Savior without interference. Evangelism that uses public pressure — requiring people to raise their hands, walk forward in a crowd, or make a public declaration — violates both human privacy and the principle of non-meritorious faith. The merit in salvation lies entirely with the object, the Lord Jesus Christ, not with any action of the one believing. True faith is an act of the will in the privacy of the soul.

The state must neither coerce acceptance of Christ nor punish rejection of Him. No church has the authority to persecute those who reject Christ as Savior. The state must never adopt an official religion supported by public taxation; all religious bodies must be free from taxation and free from state support equally. The separation of church and state is therefore not an anti-religious principle but a foundational establishment principle protecting the very freedom that makes genuine evangelism possible.

The alternative is visible in the historical record of regions where a state church held coercive power. The dominance of a state church destroys religious freedom; the resulting resentment and reaction leave populations unable to conceptualize an alternative other than the opposite extreme. The doctrine of John 3:36 frames the issue with absolute clarity: 'He that believeth on the Son hath everlasting life; he that believeth not the Son shall not see life, but the wrath of God abideth on him.' The choice is binary and entirely private. Establishment exists to ensure that choice is genuinely free.

Conclusions from Chapter Three Hundred Eighty-Three

1. The plan of God operates in three sequential stages. Stage One (X radical) establishes the human condition at physical birth and the potential of salvation. Stage Two (Y radical) encompasses the judicial imputations of salvation and the believer's advance toward maturity. Stage Three (Z radical) is the supergrace life with its eternal rewards. Each stage carries its own hope — its own absolute confidence — that generates appropriate action.

2. All blessing from God flows from the justice of God to the righteousness of God. Justice and righteousness together constitute divine integrity. The justice of God is the pipeline through which all blessing is dispensed. No blessing comes through works, personality, morality, or sacrifice. Blessing comes through doctrine resident in the soul, which provides capacity for the divine blessing that justice imputes to righteousness.

3. The family is the third divine institution, designed to bridge helplessness at birth and responsibility in adult life. Parental authority is the essential mechanism of this bridge. Authority training — instilling respect for the privacy of others, for property, for law and order, and for legitimate government — must begin in the home. It cannot be deferred. Christian parents bear an additional responsibility to evangelize their children and to model respect for the teaching authority of the Word of God.

4. The nation is the fourth divine institution, designed to protect human freedom. The division of humanity into distinct national entities at Babel was a divine judgment against internationalism and a protective design for the perpetuation of history. Internationalism in any form — political, civic, or religious — is outside the authorization of divine establishment for this stage of history.

5. Racial ideology has no foundation in the historical record. As civilization developed, racial distinctions were obliterated through migration, conquest, and intermarriage. The populations of every historically developed nation are composites. Racial purity is a myth; its use as political ideology is a form of expediency that has no support from the Word of God.

6. Nations aligned with divine establishment exhibit seven identifiable characteristics. These are: interior protection of freedom through honorable law enforcement and jurisprudence; exterior protection through an honorable military; a government that protects rather than destroys freedom; a free-enterprise economy; a system of common law that restrains crime without exceeding its proper function; a national culture reflecting integrity and patriotism; and a government administration that exercises authority within its proper limits.

7. Law must not be weaponized as an instrument for solving social problems. The proper function of law is to restrain criminal action and protect the freedom, rights, life, and property of individuals. Legislation that invades private associations, coerces private economic decisions, or redistributes personal property under the claim of advancing the common good exceeds the proper scope of law and becomes a form of oppression.

8. Democracy is incompatible with the standards of divine establishment. A republic — a government of enumerated powers and constitutional limits — is compatible with Scripture. Democracy, governed by numerical majority opinion, is not. Majority opinion carries no authority as a standard of truth or justice. Every democracy in history has tended toward anarchy without the restraining structure of constitutional government.

9. The laws of divine establishment exist to protect the freedom that makes genuine evangelism possible. Where people are free — free to accept Christ, free to reject Him, free from coercion in either direction — the gospel can be heard and believed in the privacy of the soul. Evangelism that depends on public pressure or crowd psychology violates both human privacy and the principle of non-meritorious faith. The state must neither coerce religious belief nor punish religious choice. Separation of church and state is a biblical establishment principle, not an anti-religious one.

10. The separation of church and state protects the integrity of both institutions. A state religion always destroys human freedom. Where a church holds coercive state power, it destroys the very freedom of conscience that genuine faith requires. History demonstrates that populations long subjected to coercive state religion become unable to conceive of genuine religious freedom and are therefore susceptible to the opposite extreme. Establishment law, properly applied, prevents this outcome.

Glossary

Glossary

Term Greek / Transliteration Definition

These laws make possible human freedom within the framework of authority. They operate in the X radical of the plan of God and apply to believers and unbelievers alike.

There are no Christian nations as such; a client nation is an establishment nation that contains a functioning pivot of mature believers.
Pivot The body of mature believers within a national entity whose adjustment to the justice of God sustains divine blessing on that nation. The size and health of the pivot determines the degree to which a nation continues to receive logistical grace at the national level.

Imputation The divine act of crediting something to someone's account. Seven key imputations structure the plan of God: (1) human life to the soul at birth; (2) Adam's original sin to the old sin nature; (3) personal sins to Christ on the cross; (4) divine righteousness to the believer at salvation; (5) eternal life to the believer at salvation; (6) divine blessing to the believer at maturity; (7) rewards and blessings at the judgment seat of Christ.
Old sin nature (OSN) The sin capacity inherited at physical birth through the male genetic line. Adam's original sin is imputed to the genetically formed old sin nature. Personal sins accumulate in the OSN but are not imputed to the individual for condemnation — they were judged in Christ on the cross.
